title: Geometric-specialization category and codimension
statement: For a scheme $S$, geometric points $p:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_p\to S$ with $\Omega_p$ algebraically closed [def-weil-geometric-point] form the geometric-specialization category: a morphism $p\to q$ is an $S$-morphism $S_{(p)}\to S_{(q)}$ of their strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], with identity and composition those of schemes over $S$. Thus an isomorphism means an isomorphism of strict localizations over $S$, not an isomorphism of the arbitrary algebraically closed overfields. The underlying point of $p$ is its image in $S$; its distinguished point in $S_{(p)}$ is the image of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_p$ under the canonical evaluation map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation]. Each arrow is identified with the strict-local specialization datum of [def-trf-specialization-slice-data]. Its codimension is the Krull dimension of the reduced closure of the image of this distinguished source point in $S_{(q)}$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]; equivalently it is the topological Krull dimension of that closure, since reduction leaves the topological space unchanged. It is immediate if this dimension is one.
